Thirteen years of volunteer work—and a Texas classic is flying again. ✈️🔧

The Commemorative Air Force Houston Wing’s L-17 Navion returned to flight on September 8, with Matt Brzostowski at the controls. General Aviation News featured the milestone October 22, following the CAF’s October 14 announcement.

This comeback took much more than a fresh coat of paint. Corrosion meant the original wings couldn’t be saved, so the team sourced replacement wings from a donor aircraft. Volunteers also upgraded the engine and propeller and worked through fuel-system, brake, landing-gear, interior and instrument tasks.

The flying has resumed, but the finishing work continues. The Wing plans a Korean War-era Army olive-drab paint scheme after engine break-in flights and additional pilot checkouts, with a new look and official name hoped for in early 2027.

Here’s to the people who keep showing up at the hangar until “someday” becomes a flight. 💙
